thought_title: Greetings in His Flesh and Blood

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἐν Τρωάδι, ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν διὰ Βούρρου, ὅν ἀπεστείλατε μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἅμα Ἐφεσίοις, τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὑμῶν, ὃς κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν. καὶ ὄφελον πάντες αὐτὸν ἐμιμοῦντο, ὄντα ἐξεμπλάριον θεοῦ διακονίας. ἀμείψεται αὐτὸν ἡ χάρις κατὰ πάντα. [2] ἀσπάζομαι τὸν ἀξιόθεον ἐπίσκοπον καὶ θεοπρεπὲς πρεσβυτέριον καὶ τοὺς συνδούλους μου διακόνους καὶ τοὺς κατ’ ἄνδρα καὶ κοινῇ πάντας ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ αἵματι, πάθει τε καὶ ἀναστάσει σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ, ἐν ἑνότητι θεοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν. χάρις ὑμῖν, ἕλεος, εἰρήνη, ὑπομονὴ διὰ παντός.
pass_a_gloss: [1] The love of the brothers in Troas greets you; from there I am also writing to you through Burrhus, whom you sent with me together with the Ephesians, your brothers, and who refreshed me in every way. And I wish all would imitate him, since he is a model of service to God. Grace will repay him in everything. [2] I greet the bishop worthy of God, and the godly presbytery, and the deacons, my fellow servants, and all of you, one by one and together, in the name of Jesus Christ and in his flesh and blood, in his suffering and resurrection, both of flesh and of spirit, in the unity of God and of you. Grace to you, mercy, peace, endurance, always.
pass_b_english: Greetings to you from the love of the brothers in Troas. It is from Troas, too, that I write to you, by means of Burrhus. You sent him with me, along with the Ephesians, your brothers, and he has given me rest at every turn. If only all would imitate him, for he is a pattern of service to God! Grace will repay him in all things.

My greetings go to the bishop worthy of God, to the presbytery fit for God, and to my fellow servants the deacons; to all of you, one by one and all together, in the name of Jesus Christ, in his flesh and his blood, in his passion and his resurrection, of flesh and of spirit alike, in the oneness of God and of you. Grace be with you, and mercy, peace, and endurance, at all times.

choices.why: ἀδελφῶν rendered literally; no inclusive expansion added in the reading text.
rejected: brothers and sisters (adds to the Greek)

choices.english: for he is a pattern of service to God
choices.why: Latin loanword 'exemplar' rendered as plain 'pattern'; the participle ὄντα kept as a reason ('for he is').
rejected: exemplar of the ministry of God (stiff)

choices.why: Ignatius's flesh-and-spirit pairing kept; it qualifies the passion and resurrection.

choices.english: worthy of God … fit for God
choices.why: Two Ignatian compounds with θεός, kept distinct.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF's 'most worthy' and 'very venerable' drop the 'God' element in ἀξιόθεος and θεοπρεπής.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 12 (sections 1, 2); old ANF span covers the full chapter.
Pack topic: passion-resurrection. Same chapter English is shared by every excerpt id on this chapter.
Burrhus also appears in Ephesians 2 and Philadelphians 11 of Ignatius.

Repair 2026-10-02 (round 2): 'brothers' for ἀδελφῶν; καί restored ('from Troas, too'); 'by the hand of' and 'your' removed; σύνδουλοι kept as 'my fellow servants'; ὄντα kept as a reason. ὅθεν ('from where') = Troas, where Ignatius is writing, so 'from Troas' names the place the relative points to.

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] against A and B. Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἐν Τρωάδι matches A “The love of the brothers in Troas greets you” and B “Greetings to you from the love of the brothers in Troas”; ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν διὰ Βούρρου matches A “from there I am also writing to you through Burrhus” and B “from Troas, too, that I write to you, by means of Burrhus”; ὅν ἀπεστείλατε μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἅμα Ἐφεσίοις, τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὑμῶν, ὃς κατὰ πάντα με ἀνέπαυσεν keeps you as senders and Burrhus as the one who refreshed/gave rest. ὄφελον πάντες αὐτὸν ἐμιμοῦντο stays a wish (A “I wish all would imitate him”; B “If only all would imitate him”); ἀμείψεται αὐτὸν ἡ χάρις κατὰ πάντα keeps Grace as future agent in both. Section [2] ἀσπάζομαι τὸν ἀξιόθεον ἐπίσκοπον καὶ θεοπρεπὲς πρεσβυτέριον καὶ τοὺς συνδούλους μου διακόνους … σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ αἵματι, πάθει τε καὶ ἀναστάσει σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ, ἐν ἑνότητι θεοῦ καὶ ὑμῶν and χάρις ὑμῖν, ἕλεος, εἰρήνη, ὑπομονὴ διὰ παντός are present in both without reversal. No citation appears in the locked text. Title names the flesh-and-blood greeting, not only the locus.
